error.signature: AI cites a fixed dollar/lira figure (e.g. $85-115, 3,000-4,000 TL) as the current fee to register a foreign phone brought into Turkey past the 120-day grace period
error.regex: (imei kayıt|imei registration fee|yurt dışı telefon.*(harç|ücret)|turkey.*phone.*register.*120 day|foreign phone.*turkey.*(register|fee))

verdict.summary: Turkey requires foreign phones used with a local SIM for more than 120 cumulative days to be registered with BTK (the telecom regulator) and a 'harç' (fee) paid, or the device is blocked from all three Turkish networks. The fee is not fixed: it is Tariff 8 of the Fees Law (492 sayılı Harçlar Kanunu), reset every January 1 by the Ministry of Treasury and Finance's Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı using the prior year's statutory revaluation rate. For 2026, the Harçlar Kanunu Genel Tebliği (Seri No: 98), published in the Official Gazette on 31 December 2025, fixed it at 54,258.00 TL - far above the ~$85-115 (3,000-4,000 TL) figures still circulating in older English-language guides. Separately, BTK limits each passport to registering one device per 3 calendar years.

dead_ends.action: Cite a fixed dollar/lira figure (e.g. $85-115 or 3,000-4,000 TL) as this year's fee for registering a foreign phone used in Turkey past 120 days
dead_ends.why_fails: The fee is a 'harç' under Tariff 8 of Turkey's Fees Law (492 sayılı Harçlar Kanunu), reset every January 1st by the Ministry of Treasury and Finance's Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı using the prior year's statutory revaluation rate (18.95% for 2026, itself building on a 25.49% 2025 revaluation). The Harçlar Kanunu Genel Tebliği (Seri No: 98), Official Gazette, 31 December 2025, fixes the 'Yolcu beraberinde getirilen telefon kullanım izin harcı' at 54,258.00 TL for 2026 - roughly fifteen times the $85-115 figure still repeated in older English-language travel guides. An AI answer trained on that older data understates the fee by an order of magnitude.
dead_ends.condition: Registering a foreign phone in 2026 or later
dead_ends.common_misconception: That the registration fee is a small, mostly-static customs charge rather than an annually re-priced tax that compounds with Turkey's inflation-linked revaluation rate.

dead_ends.action: Assume a traveler can register a new personal device on the same passport again soon after a previous registration, e.g. after upgrading phones
dead_ends.why_fails: BTK's Central Device Registration System (Merkezi Cihaz Kayıt Sistemi) limits each passport to bringing in one device per 3 calendar years ('3 takvim yılı içerisinde 1 adet cihazın yurda getirilebileceği'); after one registration, no new registration right exists until January 1 two years later. A second device registered on the same passport within that window is disconnected from Turkish networks after its own 120-day window.
dead_ends.condition: Second foreign device on the same passport within 3 calendar years
dead_ends.common_misconception: That the 120-day/registration rule applies per device with no limit on how many devices one passport can register.

workarounds.action: Check the current-year fee directly from the annual Harçlar Kanunu Genel Tebliği (or a Turkish accountancy/tax portal that mirrors it) before budgeting, rather than reusing a figure from a prior year or an English-language blog
workarounds.how: Search for the current year's 'Harçlar Kanunu Genel Tebliği' and look up Tariff 8, section VIII ('Yolcu beraberinde getirilen telefon kullanım izin harcı').
workarounds.condition: Planning to keep and use a foreign phone in Turkey past 120 days

workarounds.action: If staying long-term, buy a phone from a Turkish retailer instead of registering one brought from abroad - domestically sold phones already carry a valid Turkish IMEI and are exempt from this registration process and fee entirely
workarounds.condition: Long-term stay or digital-nomad visa holder
workarounds.tradeoff: Loses use of a phone already owned; involves the up-front cost of a new device.
